Pavlohrad Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Pavlohrad's Jewish population peaked at 11,647 in 1910, supporting five synagogues, a talmud-torah, and extensive commercial holdings, including all three of the town's drug stores. Pogroms in 1918 and 1919 drove many Jews away, and the population nearly halved by 1920. Josef Yakovlevich Kotin, a significant Soviet armored vehicle design engineer and chief designer of the KV and IS series heavy tanks, was born in Pavlohrad in 1908. Under German occupation from October 1941, Jews were held in a labor camp before being moved to Mavrino and murdered between November 1941 and January 1942; 3,700 people from Pavlohrad and the surrounding area were killed in total, most of them Jewish.
